notes: EW IEM G4 is a bundled system: an SR IEM G4 half-rack stereo transmitter (1U-ish, 1.7" tall, needs the included GA 3 kit for standard 19" rack mounting or pairs with a second half-rack unit) + an EK IEM G4 bodypack receiver + IE 4 earphones. Ports above are drawn from both units: Audio In 1/2, AF Out/Phones, Ethernet, Antenna Output, and DC In belong to the rack-mountable SR IEM G4 transmitter; Earphone Out belongs to the body-worn EK IEM G4 receiver. The EK receiver itself has no external DC/charging port — it runs on 2x AA batteries or a Sennheiser BA 2015 rechargeable accupack (charged in a separate external charger, not modeled here). No "type" enum value matches "wireless in-ear monitor" exactly; "Wireless mic" was chosen as the closest fit since it's the same evolution-wireless G4 RF hardware family, even though signal direction is opposite (feeds IEMs rather than capturing a mic signal). Antenna Output and Ethernet intentionally carry no "grade" — BNC here is RF antenna feed (not SDI), and the source does not state an Ethernet link speed. Specs confirmed on the A1 (470–516 MHz) SKU; other regional frequency variants (A: 516–558 MHz, G: 566–608 MHz, etc.) share identical physical I/O — only tunable RF range differs. Sennheiser's own product/spec pages (sennheiser.com, sennheiser-hearing.com) returned 404/redirect errors during this research session, so B&H's detailed spec table (which mirrors Sennheiser's published data sheet organization by System/Receiver/Transmitter/Earphones) was used as the authoritative source instead.
